fields.statement: Pre-publish audit at 5d28d354 (main plus this branch), amended on attempt 2. SCANNER: gitleaks 8.18.4 with default rules over full history (`gitleaks detect --log-opts=--all`, 887 commits, 6.9s): no leaks found; the attempt-1 verifier re-ran it over history (888 commits) and the tree (--no-git) with the same clean result. MANUAL SWEEP of HEAD (git grep over tree, .rhiza/log, .rhiza/rendered incl. Sources and session notes) for password/secret/api key/private key/ghp_/github_pat_/sk-/sk-ant-/AKIA/xox tokens, emails (`git grep -hoE '<email regex>' HEAD | sort | uniq -c`), IPs, home paths, private hostnames, phone numbers; and history for deleted .env/.pem/.key/.db/credentials files and blobs over 1 MB: no secrets or credentials found (only hits: a GITHUB_TOKEN secret reference in release.yml, the word 'secret' in scrub docs and a test fixture SECRET-RAW; the two 1 MB blobs are describe-golden.txtar). FINDINGS: (1) docs/rex-upstream/notification-banner.md named the owner's private tailnet HTTPS hostname: FIXED in commit 36850ef3 (now 'a tailnet HTTPS name'); it remains in earlier history. (2) Two of the owner's personal email addresses (the gmail one and the hey.com full-name one): ACCEPTED, no action; they are the git author/committer identity of 913 commits and appear in Actor records in .rhiza/log, so they are public once the repo is, removable only by a history rewrite. (3) A third owner address (the short hey.com one) was used as a sample email in internal/textref/textref.go (doc comment) and internal/textref/textref_test.go (two test inputs): FIXED in the publish-audit attempt-2 commit, replaced by ada@example.com (go test ./internal/textref passes). Capability text-ref-syntax's acceptance named it as well: FIXED going forward in review cycle 2 by a set of that acceptance in this change set (now ada@example.com, matching the code), which clears it from the current render of text-ref-syntax. It remains in 8 .rhiza/log entries of the text-references change set 01M6HNNWFR1J2AHQRNKFTPME46, in the 4 evidence renders derived from them (text-ref-syntax-qa-2, text-ref-syntax-verified, -verified-2, -verified-3; evidence statements record what was run and are not rewritten), and in older history of the two Go files: ACCEPTED as a public contact address; only a history rewrite removes it from .rhiza/log (append-only) and git history. (4) A Tailscale CGNAT address and the owner's machine name in three session notes (and their log entries and renders): ACCEPTED as low risk (reachable only inside the owner's tailnet); not edited because .rhiza/log is append-only and renders derive from it. (5) The owner's macOS username in absolute home paths in 18 files (log entries, renders, evidence): ACCEPTED, discloses a username only. (6) Other emails, IPs and hosts found (test@rhiza.invalid, me@x.org and x@*.example in test fixtures, a 192.168.x test fixture, daemon.home file name, example.com/example.test/invalid addresses) are test fixtures or file names, not private hosts. ONLY A HISTORY REWRITE WOULD REMOVE: the owner emails in every commit's author/committer fields; the tailnet hostname in older versions of notification-banner.md; the third owner address in older versions of textref.go/textref_test.go and in the text-references change set's .rhiza/log entries; and findings 4 and 5 in .rhiza/log (append-only) and its history. Recommendation: none of these is a credential; the owner decides whether to publish as is. The owner reads this before flipping visibility.

set.acceptance: Unit tests in internal/textref: a reference starts with @ at the start of the text or after whitespace or an opening ( or [ and is followed by a handle (lower-case words joined by single dashes) or an ID or 4+ character ID prefix; ada@example.com, checkout@v7 and '@key' contain no reference; @@ yields a literal @ and is never a reference; the resolver returns @@{<full ID>} as unresolved and flagged escaped and an @{<full ID>} the lookup does not map as unresolved, writes both as @<full ID> without braces so the formatter shows neither as a reference, and still turns @@{ID} into the literal @{ID}; a resolver given a lookup rewrites every reference, @{<ID>} included, to @{<full ID>} and returns each unresolved one with its offset, so @{BOGUS} is unresolved; a formatter treats only @{<26-character ID>} in stored text as a reference, shows it as @<handle> when the lookup gives a live node's handle and as @{<full ID>} when the node is retired or the lookup has none, and treats stored '@{ID}', '@{BOGUS}' and '@{<full ID>}' as literal text shown as '@@{ID}' etc.; and shows a stored literal @ that would start a reference (from @@word) as @@; a fuzz test checks that formatting resolved text, literal @ included, and resolving it again yields the same stored text
